summary.text: Alan Bradstock is the Democratic nominee for Pennsylvania's 14th District. A Donora native, he describes a career as a U.S. Army aviation officer who deployed during Operation Desert Storm, a 20-year FBI special agent, and later a KPMG auditor, financial adviser and intelligence-community contractor. This is his first run for elected office; his campaign emphasizes economic security, health care, veterans and limiting money in politics.

paragraphs.text: Bradstock is a native of Donora, Pennsylvania, and a graduate of Ringgold High School in Washington County, according to his campaign website.

He earned a bachelor's degree in accounting from Washington & Jefferson College, graduating cum laude and Phi Beta Kappa, and played four years of basketball there; he was recently inducted into the college's Athletics Hall of Fame.
After college, Bradstock was commissioned as a U.S. Army aviation officer and served eight years.

His campaign says he was stationed in Germany during the fall of the Berlin Wall, deployed to the Middle East during Operation Desert Storm and earned a master's degree in international relations through Troy State University's overseas program.

He then spent two decades as an FBI special agent: after New Agent Training at Quantico he worked drug, public-corruption, kidnapping and violent-crime cases in Las Cruces, New Mexico, became a Counterterrorism Division supervisor with assignments at CIA Headquarters and the DEA's Special Operations Division, and later served in Louisville, Kentucky.
He also served as Deputy Legal Attaché at the U.S. Embassy in Ottawa, working with Canadian law enforcement and intelligence agencies.

In the private sector, Bradstock worked as an auditor for KPMG, as an independent financial adviser, and as a contractor supporting the U.S. Intelligence Community in budget, strategy and program management.
He announced his candidacy in November 2025, and WESA reported it is his first run for elected office.
He was unopposed in the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary (48,774 votes).
According to his campaign website, he lives in Fayette County with his wife and has two children.
